source_facts.fact: The Mining Remediation Authority dataset describes areas with one or more recorded mining-related features at surface or shallow depth and says new development proposals should be supported by a Coal Mining Risk Assessment; dataset was updated 14 April 2026.
source_facts.gate: High-risk-area membership is a screening trigger, not proof of instability at an exact building footprint.

source_facts.fact: Mining Remediation Authority policy says building over or within the influencing distance of a mine entry should wherever possible be avoided and requires suitable engineering evidence and permissions where considered.
source_facts.gate: Mapped mine-entry influence is not a final geotechnical design or planning outcome.

source_facts.fact: Planning guidance says developers should obtain appropriate technical advice and undertake necessary investigations where instability is known or suspected.
source_facts.gate: National guidance does not provide a parcel stability value without investigation.

source_facts.fact: Environment Agency's historic-landfill dataset was updated 15 May 2026, is updated every six months, can be incomplete for pre-licensing sites and covers sites where no environmental permit is in force.
source_facts.gate: Dataset intersection is screening evidence, not a current contamination determination or permit status for every activity.

source_facts.fact: The Indicative Atlas version 3 was updated 23 July 2026 and classes each 1 km grid square by the highest radon potential found within it; the dataset is explicitly indicative rather than definitive.
source_facts.gate: Grid classification cannot replace property-specific radon testing or site design assessment.

source_facts.fact: Approved Document C covers site preparation, unsuitable material, contaminants, sub-soil drainage and moisture resistance under Building Regulations in England.
source_facts.gate: Building-regulation guidance is not planning permission or a parcel contamination clearance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Coal Development High Risk Area dataset update
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mining Remediation Authority dataset last updated 14 April 2026 and combines recorded coal-mining related surface/shallow features.

official_measurement_examples.name: CMRA planning trigger semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: For most development in the Development High Risk Area a Coal Mining Risk Assessment is required, subject to listed exemptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Mine-entry precautionary policy
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building over or within influence of mine entries should wherever possible be avoided; engineering and permissions are required where pursued.

official_measurement_examples.name: Land stability planning scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Known or suspected instability requires early technical assessment and necessary investigations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Historic landfill update cycle
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic Landfill Sites updated 15 May 2026 and normally every six months; pre-licensing information may be incomplete.

official_measurement_examples.name: Historic landfill permit semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic landfill means no environmental permit is in force; the Environment Agency is not regulator for historic landfills.

core_rules: Development High Risk Area is a screening area not proof of parcel instability
Development Low Risk Area does not prove absence of unrecorded mining hazards
CMRA requirement is not an automatic refusal of development
CMRA exemption must be checked by application type and must not be assumed
coalfield membership is not the same as Development High Risk Area membership
mine-entry records require site-specific location confirmation where material
mine-entry influence distance is an engineering concern not a cadastral boundary
mapped mine-entry influence is not a final foundation design
building over mine entries should not be assumed acceptable after capping
Mining Remediation Authority advice is not planning permission
Mining Remediation Authority permission is not local planning permission
coal-mining report availability is not a geotechnical survey
historic abandonment plans can be incomplete and must not imply total mine certainty
coal-mining archive records must remain date- and source-specific
land stability guidance is not a parcel stability measurement
absence of recorded instability does not prove future stability
landslide subsidence and ground heave must remain distinct mechanisms
ground investigation results cannot be fabricated from regional mapping
planning conditions for investigation are not evidence investigation has occurred
remediation requirement is not evidence remediation is complete
Part 2A contaminated-land determination is distinct from planning contamination assessment
potential contamination is not statutory contaminated-land determination
former land use alone does not prove contamination concentration
contamination source pathway receptor assessment requires site-specific evidence
planning suitability after remediation cannot be inferred without verification
voluntary remediation advice is not regulatory approval or planning permission
controlled-waters impact requires site-specific evidence
historic landfill polygon intersection is not proof of current pollution
historic landfill is distinct from currently authorised landfill
historic landfill data can be incomplete for pre-licensing sites
dataset update cycle must be retained when using landfill records
landfill boundary digitisation scale is not a parcel survey
waste type history is not current soil chemistry
environmental permit status is not planning permission
landfill engineering permit requirements apply to operators and not automatically to adjacent parcels
hydrogeological risk assessment cannot be inferred from landfill proximity alone
landfill gas risk requires site-specific assessment
radon potential is not a measured property radon concentration
1 km radon grid square is not cadastral geometry
highest potential within a radon grid must not be copied to every building as measured value
radon affected-area status is a testing and design trigger not planning refusal
radon Action Level is not evidence a specific property exceeds it
building regulation radon measures must not be treated as completed construction
Approved Document C compliance is not planning consent
building-regulation guidance and planning guidance must remain separate
screening datasets are not remediation cost estimates
NO_DATA cannot be converted into no ground risk
no parcel geotechnical result contamination clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
